reading: Separator lines cut the grid into a lattice of equal panels. One panel holds a shape; every panel in each panel-row gets a copy of that shape, coloured with the colour of the square in that row's first panel (which it replaces).
verb: stamp shape into every panel, coloured per row

slots.panels: cells of the lattice cut by full separator lines (separator colour kept)
slots.unit: the pattern of the one panel whose content differs from the plain square (the shape)
slots.colour: for each panel-row, the colour of the square in its first panel
slots.placement: same relative position inside every panel, replacing the old content

why: every panel of row r equals the shape pattern recoloured to row r's square colour; separators unchanged

reading: Panels come in left/right pairs separated by background lines. Within each pair the two shapes swap panels, each keeping its position and being drawn in the background colour of the panel it came from (so if both panels share a background, both shapes vanish).

slots.panels: blocks of one background colour cut by all-0 rows and columns, taken in left/right pairs
slots.subject: the shape (non-panel-background cells) in each panel
slots.destination: the other panel of the pair, same relative position
slots.colour: the background colour of the source panel

why: out left panel = panel bg with right shape mask in right bg colour, and vice versa; separators unchanged

reading: One large shape is built from k-by-k solid blocks among scattered noise pixels of a second colour. Output is the shape downscaled by k (one cell per block) and drawn in the noise colour.
verb: downscale shape and recolour to noise colour

slots.subject: the colour forming the large block-structured shape (its bounding box)
slots.scale: block size k (largest uniform square cell size)
slots.output: box/k grid: cell = colour if block is filled, else 0

why: output cell (i,j) is noise colour iff block (i,j) of the shape's box is filled

reading: A key in the corner shows colour pairs a->b (two-colour component). Each other shape of colour a gets its bounding box grown by one cell, and every background cell in that box that is reachable from outside the shape (not an enclosed hole) is painted key(a).
verb: halo each shape in its key colour

slots.key: two-colour components in the corner: left colour a -> right colour b
slots.subject: each single-colour object whose colour appears as a key source
slots.region: background cells inside the object's bbox expanded by 1, 4-connected to the box edge (enclosed holes excluded)

why: only those halo cells change, each to key(a); shapes, holes and key unchanged

reading: The output is the input scaled up as a fractal: block (i,j) of the output is a copy of the input where input cell (i,j) is foreground, else empty.
why: each output block is the input or all background, exactly at the fg cells of the input

reading: Two 2x2 squares: from the blue (1) square a diagonal ray of 1 runs up-left from its top-left corner to the border; from the red (2) square a diagonal ray of 2 runs down-right from its bottom-right corner to the border.
why: each ray starts at the square's outer corner, direction fixed per colour (1: up-left, 2: down-right), and stops at the grid border

reading: Three same-colour points lie on a diagonal with equal spacing d. Draw concentric square rings centred on the middle point at Chebyshev distances 0, d, 2d, ... clipped by the grid.

slots.centre: the middle of the three markers
slots.extent: rings until they leave the grid (clipped at border)

why: cell is colour iff its Chebyshev distance to the centre is a multiple of d
invariants: the three markers lie on rings

reading: Two separator columns (6) cut the input into three equal panels. Output is one panel-sized grid spliced from them: the left columns from panel 1, the middle column(s) from panel 2, the right columns from panel 3 (for width 5: 2+1+2).

slots.panels: three stripes cut by full separator columns

reading: A single marker cell shoots diagonal lines of its own colour in all four diagonal directions until the grid border.
why: every diagonal from the marker reaches the border; nothing else changes

reading: One 8-coloured blob is a tiling of 2x2 squares and 3-cell L pieces; each piece is recoloured by its type: 2x2 square -> 1, L missing top-left -> 2, L missing bottom-left -> 3, L missing top-right -> 4.
verb: decompose into pieces and colour by piece shape

slots.subject: the 8 cells, partitioned into 2x2 squares and L-trominoes (2x2 minus one corner)
slots.key: piece shape -> colour: square 1, missing TL 2, missing BL 3, missing TR 4

why: every 8 cell becomes the colour of the piece it belongs to; no other cell changes
